newsitem.title: GERMANY: German roaster Tchibo announces retail price hike.
newsitem.headline: German roaster Tchibo announces retail price hike.

text.p: German coffee roaster Tchibo Frisch-Roest Kaffee GmbH on Friday said it had raised its retail prices by up to one mark per 500 grams with immediate effect.
"The average increase is just under one mark," said a spokesman.
Flagship product Feine Milde, which has a 10 percent share in the Tchibo product mix now costs 9.49 marks, and Tchibo's average price should be just under 10 marks.
Tchibo cited fresh coffee rallies in the world market on concern about Latin American supply and low consumer stocks.
Tchibo also said the strong dollar was increasing mark-based buying-in prices and the dollar firmness looked set to continue.
Tchibo's announcement followed a statement earlier today from market leader Kraft Jacobs Suchard (KJS), part of Philip Morris, it was considering a price hike within a week.
Tchibo is the second largest roaster after KJS, which has a 30 percent market share.
Tchibo, which operates through tied retail outlets, can enact price rises directly while KJS can only raise ex-works prices to the trade which may or may not pass them on.
Tchibo to date in 1997 has increased its prices by 0.50 marks while roasters operating through the wholesale trade have announced price increases by 2.50 marks.
But they have not been achieved because of competitive pressures.
Tchibo was recently given approval to buy competitor Eduscho GmbH & Co KG retroactive to January 1, 1997, which gives it an estimated 25-26 percent market share.
Today's announcement applied to Tchibo products.
The company expected consumers to accept the price rises.
A spokesman for Eduscho said the company was not planning further increases after it adjusted the price of the entire product range by one mark in late April.
